Synopsis:
Sterling dipped slightly vs. the dollar ahead of BoE Governor Bailey and MPC members testifying before the Treasury Select Committee. Markets are pricing a hold at 3.75% next week, though hawkish dissent risks are skewing upward — Barclays sees a possible 6-3 vote with 3 dissenters, with risk of a 4th. Catalysts include surging oil near $100/bbl driven by Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and Iran's geopolitical posturing, a surprise July hawkish dissent by Mann, and slowing retail sales. Sterling also weakened sharply vs. the yen on BoJ hawkish expectations.
